> A small custom PCB built around a Seeed XIAO RP2040. It is designed to read temperature, humidity and air pressure from a BME280 sensor and show them on a 0.96" OLED screen, with a rotary encoder to switch between pages.

## Design

### 2026-11-01: Objective: Design a custom compact microcontroller-based sensor module featuring a display and sensor peripherals, transitioning the circuit from schematic capture to physical board layout (PCB).

**10h**

Objective: Design a custom compact microcontroller-based sensor module featuring a display and sensor peripherals, transitioning the circuit from schematic capture to physical board layout (PCB).

1. Schematic Capture & Component Selection
Microcontroller Integration: Placed and wired the core microcontroller unit, establishing proper power connections, decoupling capacitors, and designated communication lines (such as I2C data and clock lines).

Peripherals & Modules: Integrated sensor modules and display interfaces into the schematic, ensuring correct pin mappings for power, ground, and data buses.

Electrical Rules Check (ERC): Ran a complete ERC to verify that all power flags, pins, and net labels were properly connected without floating nodes or conflicting outputs.

2. PCB Layout & Routing
Board Outline & Placement: Defined a clean, compact rectangular board outline. Optimized component placement to keep signal paths short and minimize trace crossings.

Routing: Routed the front copper (F.Cu) traces carefully, ensuring appropriate trace widths for power and signal lines.

Ground Plane: Added a solid copper pour (GND fill) on the back copper layer (B.Cu) to improve signal integrity and reduce electrical noise.

Design Rules Check (DRC): Executed a final DRC to ensure zero clearance errors, overlapping pads, or unrouted connections before generating the manufacturing files.
